prerequisites: Partial completion of learning objectives for Technologies and Programming Paradigms
Partial completion of learning objectives for Human-Computer Interaction
Partial completion of learning objectives for Databases
Partial completion of learning objectives for Software Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to select, design, deploy, integrate, evaluate, build, manage, exploit and maintain hardware, software and network technologies, within appropriate cost and quality parameters.
Ability to select, deploy, integrate and manage information systems that meet the needs of the organization, with identified cost and quality criteria.
Ability to conceive systems, applications and services based on network technologies, including Internet, web, e-commerce, multimedia, interactive services and mobile computing.
Analyze and prepare the requirements of an interactive system with a client, producing the functional requirements part of a bid request.
Analyze, evaluate and discuss different alternatives for implementation, development and subcontracting of a software system, selecting the most appropriate for the organization's needs.
Perform technical reviews of products developed by other work teams.
Prepare an implementation and deployment plan for a software system and monitor it.
Prepare a software configuration management plan and control versions and changes.
Prepare the strategy and integration tests of a software system.
Understand the content and objectives of the different process models, evaluation and quality standards applicable to software products and processes.
Understand the different enterprise architecture models and their relationship with the involved technologies.
Understand the different functionalities of typical packaged applications (CRM, ERP).

syllabus_topics: General process of elicitation, validation and implementation of requirements
Requirement extraction and acceptance criteria in agile methodologies (SCRUM)
Quality and Standards in Software Engineering
General concepts. Definition and Types. Standards
Software Testing. Test design. V-model (levels and types). Automation.
Software Configuration Management. Plans, Version Control (Git) and Changes
Enterprise Information Systems. Architecture and functionalities.
Execution of an Information Systems project using SCRUM. Kanban board, Definition of User Stories, Implementation, Version Control and Testing.

assessment_methods.method: Work in classroom practices and deliverables
Continuous and formative evaluation in laboratory practices
Evaluation of student contribution in laboratory practice reports and products, and final presentation

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.65 * Practices + 0.35 * Theory, provided a minimum of 4.0 out of 10 is achieved in both the theory and practices blocks. If the minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, if the ordinary call grade was not 'Not Presented' and was at least 5.0, those grades for theory and practices will be used. Otherwise, both theory and practices will be re-evaluated (written exam for theory, individual work for practices) with a minimum requirement of 5.0 out of 10 in each block. The final calculation formula remains the same, with the same minimum rules.
